title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and Shakespeare legend, has died
summary: Stewart died at age 86 after "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease."
body: Patrick Stewart, the classically-trained actor who gained worldwide fame in the 1980s as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation and later as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series, has died. A message posted on Stewart's official X account said his passing came "following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia." Stewart joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, and took his first television role a year later on the long-running British series Coronation Street. He debuted on Broadway in 1971, and subsequently appeared in several feature films. title: Modern Warfare 4's newest map is actually older than the Gen Z & Alpha teens who will play it
summary: This map can drink.
body: After 23 mainline games, there are far more Call of Duty maps than anyone can reasonably remember. That's why I'm impressed it took just one screenshot for several fans (with back pain, presumably) to clock that an upcoming Modern Warfare 4 map is actually a remake of a map that's over 20 years old. Backstab, the new 6v6 map arriving on November 6, is a dead ringer for Burgundy , first seen in Call of Duty 2 way back in 2005. That means Backstab is older than the teenagers currently playing Call of Duty—do with that information what you will. A number of people noticed this around the same time, but I'll credit Reddit user wizward64 for providing helpful visuals. (Image credit: Activision Blizzard) Apologies to the reader typing "This was a classic, show some respect!", but there's no way I would've noticed the resemblance on my own. I played Call of Duty 2 on the Xbox 360 when it was new, but not all that much multiplayer. I really like the look of the original Burgundy , though: The desaturated green grass and beige brickwork of the French countryside still looks so clean and attractive 21 years later. title: Donald Glover is heading up a PUBG live action series for Netflix
summary: The award-winning writer, actor, and musician is set to write, direct, produce, and star in the show.
body: PUBG, the battle royale that lets you wear a frying pan on your ass to keep it from getting shot off, is being made into a live action series for Netflix. Narrative isn't really PUBG's strong point, but this one might be interesting for one big reason: Donald Glover is set to write, direct, and executive produce the series, and will also star in it. Stephen Glover, Donald's brother and frequent collaborator, is also attached to the project as writer and executive producer. Glover has won numerous awards over the years for writing, acting, and music (under his stage name Childish Gambino), to the point that "list of awards and nominations received by Donald Glover" has its own remarkably lengthy Wikipedia page . Highlights include two Primetime Emmy awards, two Golden Globes, five Grammy Awards, two Peabody Awards, and five Writers Guild of America Awards. The upside of PUBG not having a strong pre-existing story like, say, Halo or Fallout is that it affords creators the opportunity to do their own thing, and as I said, that could be very interesting indeed with Glover at the helm. title: Destiny 2 unvaulting update: It sure sounds like the original Destiny is finally coming to PC
summary: The actual restoration of vaulting Destiny 2 content is still a long way off, but Bungie has big plans for the future.
body: Bungie shocked the world (or at least, it shocked the world's Destiny fans) when it un-canceled Destiny 2 in September, saying the game "is foundational to Bungie’s future" and promising to restore vaulted content and "return Destiny to its original promise." In a community update shared today, the studio revealed more about that process, and one standout point is that it sure sounds like the original Destiny is finally coming to PC. The update begins with a broad overview of what led up to the unvaulting announcement and what's happened since, a broad roadmap that breaks down into three sections—First Pass, Stretch Goals, and stuff that's probably not going to happen "for technical and/or strategic reasons"—and a progress bar: (Image credit: Bungie) It's worth noting up front that while things have been happening fairly quickly so far, the actual Great Unvaultening is still a long way off. The pre-production process is now underway and expected to run until January or February of 2027, and "from that point we expect full production will be about 12 months to fully complete the porting process," Bungie head of product Josh Deane said. title: In 2023, an anonymous modder released one of the best horror games of the decade, and they still haven't broken character
summary: MyHouse.wad barrages players with horrible things they've never experienced in a game before.
body: For a lot of people, the appeal of horror is being surprised and disturbed by something they've never seen before. In recent years, I've sourced this rare feeling from movies like Obsession, where the gender dynamics of that story made it feel a bit dangerous, or Speak No Evil, which has one of the most shocking and nihilistic endings that I can recall. I even find that freshness in a modern classic like Pearl, which isn't really scary, but contrasts a technicolour old Hollywood style with a singularly unsettling Mia Goth performance to great effect. Presented by (Image credit: Torn Banner) This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 . Fear of the unknown is more valuable to me as a viewer than seeing a really good version of something I've experienced before. In games, it's largely the same—I crave new places and themes above all else. It's why Silent Hill: Townfall, Mouthwashing, Dredge, Silent Hill f, and Still Wakes The Deep all succeeded for me. They're all set in locations or timeframes I've never seen anywhere else in games. title: 'AAA publishers are abusing early access,' Denis Dyack says, and that's making things harder for everyone else
summary: Dyack believes that games like Subnautica 2 are "skewing player expectations" for early access games.
body: Denis Dyack, known for his work on games including Blood Omen: Legacy of Kain and Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem, says big game developers are "abusing early access" by using it as a marketing tool for highly polished games that are ready for full release anyway. That, Dyack believes, has shifted expectations for early access releases overall, and made life more difficult for indie developers who rely on the process to actually get their games finished and launched. "They can put up a polished product and rake in cash," Dyack told GamesIndustry . "It's a marketing beat for them. So, that leaves players often expecting a near-perfect game that, in our opinion, defeats the purpose of early access, which is a collaborative development process based on player feedback. "AAA publishers are abusing early access, skewing player expectations in such a way that it heavily disadvantages smaller independent developers." Dyack said games like Subnautica 2 and Path of Exile are "drastically changing the landscape and players' expectations," which in turn has led to "significant barriers to entry" for less polished games like Dyack's current project, Deadhaus Sonata , which is now in early …

title: YouTuber buys and turns 32 GB of laptop DDR5 into desktop RAM for just $175
summary: They then overclocked it.
body: In this week's 'what the memory crisis is doing to people' news, a YouTuber has recently bought 32 GB of DDR5 laptop memory online and successfully converted it into memory for their desktop. Overall, it cost them just $175 ($120 for the memory and $55 for extra components). That's a bit of a bargain, as 32 GB DDR5 dual-channel memory is fetching upwards of $500 on Newegg right now. Blighted Agent took to their YouTube channel to share the process, where they purchased two SO-DIMM sticks of 16 GB DDR5 memory on Facebook Marketplace (presumably salvaged from a dead laptop). From here, they put a stick on a preheater, then removed the BIOS chip, the SPD chip and all eight of its memory chips. Buying new DDR5 DIMM PCBs and heatsinks off AliExpress, they cleaned the factory unleaded solder on the laptop memory, then soldered them onto the new PCBs. It's an impressive feat that requires reballing the memory chips with a stencil, a very precise procedure. Blighted Agent says, "You want a thin layer of flux, not too much or not too little. If you do too little, the balls might not reflow properly. If you do too much, they might bridge and cause problems". Effectively, those solder balls …

body: I don't mean to be contrarian (which is rare for me), but I've been generally unfazed by the hype for Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not that I don't think it'll be good—I'm actually damn near certain it will—it's just that none of what Rockstar has focused on so far in its marketing speaks to me all that much. Anyway, throw those equanimous sentiments out the window, because an anecdote from Edge magazine's new mondo-feature on GTA 6 has convinced me this game is actually an immersive sim, and now I'm bouncing off the walls in anticipation. title: Where to find the Hokubo region Treasure Hunt in Forza Horizon 6
summary: Track this chest to some greenhouses.
body: (Image credit: Playground Games) Key deets (Image credit: Playground Games) 🚘 The treasure chest is in central Hokubo at a greenhouse in the Shikisai-no-oka. Spring has arrived in Forza Horizon 6 's Horizon Meets series, which means a new Treasure Hunt chest to find for some seasonal points, which will help you earn some progress towards the new cars on offer. This week's treasure chest is in central Hokubo by a greenhouse at the Shikisai-no-oka—the distinctive field of colourful strips you can see on the map. To find it: Drive along the road going northwest through Shikisai-no-oka's fields. When the road turns east, look for the greenhouses on your left. The chest is between these, as shown on the map above. Head there and smash the chest to get 100,000 credits, 5,000 XP, and three Season Progress. body: The Havn HS 360 is a familiar sight. More or less the same design as the company's first case, the HS 420, it's just a touch smaller. That's no bad thing; the HS 420 earned a 90% score from me due to its ability to hide most of the ugliness that comes with the usual pile of cables and connectors behind its retro futurist style facade. I feel just as positively about this slightly shrunken version too. The HS 360 is available in two versions, with or without vertical GPU mounting; and two colours, black or white. I've here two cases for review, covering all the options, and I've decided to put them to the test with rival builds. Namely to get a feel for the process of building with the different GPU mounting solutions, but also satiate my longstanding desire to build yin and yang gaming PCs. Dark and light. AMD and Nvidia. body: Phantom Blade Zero , the highly anticipated wuxia action RPG, is finally out in the world, and if you're planning on playing it on an Nvidia graphics card, maybe consider skipping the latest Nvidia driver update. Yes, that's the opposite of developer S-Game's pre-launch advice . Today, the Phantom Blade Zero devs took to the Steam page with a post titled "Reason and Madness" recounting the history of the dev team, previous works, and how Phantom Blade Zero came to be. This is followed up with three announcements: a recommendation to download the 5 GB day one patch, encouragement to try the game on handhelds and lower-end/mid-range PCs, and, finally, advice not to use the latest Nvidia driver, 621.01. It says, "Based on our testing, version 617.42 currently offers the best experience in Phantom Blade Zero. If you’ve installed a driver newer than 617.42, we recommend rolling back to 617.42 and choosing the clean installation option. title: Where to find the Mandate Encampment Outer Gate Key in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Open the gate and explore this extra region.
body: (Image credit: S-Game Studios) The Mandate Encampment Outer Gate Key is one of the most important to find in Phantom Blade Zero , since it unlocks an entire region that's otherwise inaccessible. Though you find the gate to the Mandate Encampment when you first arrive in the Village of Lu, the key is actually towards the end of the Pangzhen area (the game's 4th region), which you visit in its second chapter. Exploring the west side of the town, you'll eventually reach Gu Wangyue, a Chinese opera singer boss. After defeating her, you can drop down the well in her arena, climb the ladder straight ahead, and you'll find the key to the Mandate Encampment on a corpse in the following room surrounded by puppet enemies. It's on the main track through Pangzhen, so you'll definitely go through this room—just make sure to pick it up when you do so you can unseal the gate. summary: Buff your healing items with healer's memories.
body: You can upgrade your medicine using healer's memories at the Green Serpent House S-Game Studios You'll also get the Green Serpent Brew when you visit for the first time S-Game Studios Upgrading medicine in Phantom Blade Zero improves the percentage of HP, damage negation, and Sha-Chi that these healing consumables replenish, which is pretty powerful, as you'd imagine. You can upgrade your medicine when you reach the Green Serpent House in west Pangzhen (the game's 4th region after the Village of Lu). You'll arrive at this location during Pangzhen's second chapter, which sees you exploring the west side of the town, specifically, after you defeat Xie Qiudong, The Divine Healer and progress down the street, where you'll spot a big house with green banners and the Green Serpent House bell. The Apprentice Healer here will upgrade your medicine using Apprentice Healer's Memories and Skilled Healer's Memories, some of which you likely will have already picked up during your explorations. You'll also get the Green Serpent Brew medicine, which removes status effects, when you visit for the first time. title: How to enter the Order's underground tavern in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Find the secret entrance during the Town of Death quest.
body: Opening the entrance to the Order's underground tavern in Phantom Blade Zero took me longer than I'd like to admit, but it's required to continue progressing through Pangzhen during the Town of Death quest. In the wine yard behind the tavern building, Soul will note that the pavilion's floor on the right is hollow—this is where the secret entrance is, so you'll want to head behind the pavilion and smash the big black jar, as in the video above. This reveals a crank which will unlock the cellar and let you inside. Similar to Weeping Creek Valley's outpost or the Crimson Forest's Thieves Camp, this is an important location in Pangzhen and a hub for many of the region's sidequests. title: All Honor Among Thieves answers in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Describe the brother's letter to The Gentle Thief.
body: The Honor Among Thieves quest in Phantom Blade Zero is relatively short—you kill an enemy in the Crimson Forest who drops a letter, which you then deliver to his brother in the Thieves Camp a little further down the trail after Jing Ye. The brother, however, can't read, and demands you answer some questions about its contents to prove it's genuine. The answers to his questions are: Stole a landowner's belt. Butterfly. The letter never said. His fate is unknown. Don't worry if you get an answer wrong, he'll just end the conversation and you'll have to talk to him again. These answers are, of course, in the letter itself. Look for the Wulin Tales section of the archive and then the 8th entry, Blood Letter from the Nimble Thief. Answer all three correctly and you'll get the Silent Wrap accessory, which reduces noise from assassinations and movement by 40%, though you can upgrade this further once you unlock polishing in the Village of Lu. title: How to enter the Crimson Manor in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Find a way into this mysterious red house below the Sha-Chi tower.
body: You need to enter three portals around Wulin to open the hanging puppet's eyes S-Game Studios After that, he'll give you his tongue, which unlocks the Crimson Manor S-Game Studios Though you find it early on, the Crimson Manor is actually a bit of endgame area in Phantom Blade Zero that you'll be able to open later on. You need the Puppet's Tongue item to unseal the door, which comes from completing The Herald's Illusion quest, finding three portals into a strange realm with a hanging puppet. Each portal opens an eye—once you have all three, he'll give you his tongue. Here's where to find each portal: The first portal is by the Puppet Testing Grounds bell in the Village of Lu (the game's 3rd region). This is at the end of the area, after you go down the well, though it's basically impossible to miss. The second portal is at the end of the Mandate Encampment area after the region boss. You'll need a key from Pangzhen to open the gate to this region near the entrance to the Village of Lu (details in the linked guide). title: All Quickhand's Request treasure locations in Phantom Blade Zero

body: You first meet Quickhand Zhang in Phantom Blade Zero 's Crimson Forest and, assuming you free him, arriving at the Thieves Camp and his first hideout, he quickly recruits you to find his counterparts and unmarked treasure in each region. I've included videos below of where to find Zhang's hideout and the jade treasure chest locations in each region, plus corresponding text entries that explain what you'll need to do to reach each in terms of battling enemies or grabbing any keys required. Crimson Forest treasure locations Reward : Flying Dagger (Phantom Edge) - Thrown knives that apply poison buildup. From the Outlaw Trap bell, head into the cave directly behind you with the butcher and the dogs to grab the Crimson Forest Tunnel Crank. Use it to unlock the grate in the floor near the bell, drop down, descend the ladder, cross the wooden bridge and defeat the second butcher and dogs, then take the left path up a slope to where you'll find the chest. This second chest is behind the locked Thieves Camp Dungeon gate. To get the key, progress through the Crimson Forest until you arrive at the Cliffside Lodge. Head upstairs to grab the cellar crank, unlock the cellar, then drop down to …

title: How to beat the Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Defeat this tricky boss and complete the second part of the Triple-Threat quest.
body: The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet is the first optional boss you can encounter in Phantom Blade Zero , but it's definitely not one you're supposed to beat when you first find it. It's definitely possible, but with no Phantom Edges and only your un-upgraded starting weapon, you don't deal anywhere near enough damage to be likely to defeat her, and won't for a while. Here are some tips that'll help you best her when you're ready: Return later : There's no rush to defeat this boss or complete the Triple Threat quest. Defeating her doesn't give you a weapon or anything that's useful in the early game, either, so there's really no reason to bang your head against the fight. To beat her when you first meet her, you basically have to no-hit the entire thing, so it's not really worth it. As you can see in the video above, I returned later in the game and the fight was much more manageable. Upgrade your weapon and polish your accessories : In particular, I recommend the Ancient Armor Fragment, Jewel's Knot, and Resonance Talisman for increased damage negation, HP, and Sha-Chi. Also upgrade your weapon—remember you can buy extra materials from vendors. Upgrading your weapon will also unlock n…

title: Phantom Blade Zero's best weapon might just be the first one you get
summary: Bleed's back on the menu, boys.
body: (Image credit: S-Game Studios) Why is bleed always so strong? I guess the entire concept of dealing damage, but also building a status bar on an enemy that deals even more damage when it reaches full, is a bit OP as ideas go. Anyone who's played Elden Ring for any length of time has likely experienced Reduvia and Rivers of Blood, most likely when Nerijus invaded and wiped out their health bar in the starting area. Well, Phantom Blade Zero also has an extremely strong bleed weapon early in the game: Jagged Steel, which you get from the first boss you face (who also happens to be called Jagged Steel). During this boss fight, you'll experience the joys of bleed first hand while trying to block him, but this sword is well worth it: Its central weapon mechanic is Blood Blade, a stackable buff that increases bleed buildup and damage. At Level 5, it gets a special attack against guard-broken enemies which grants a Blood Blade stack. At Level 10 it gets more bleed buildup. At Level 15, you can charge a slash to build stacks of Blood Blade before unleashing them. At Level 20, it gets even more bleed buildup. And this isn't mentioning its powered-up left trigger combo which unleashes a flur…

title: How to complete Whence the Weeping in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Find the source of the weeping and discover its mysteries.
body: Whence the Weeping might seem like a sidequest you're supposed to complete in Phantom Blade Zero 's first Weeping Creek Valley area, but it's actually a major quest that takes a significant portion of the game to finish. If you've just started and are here wondering if you've missed something: you haven't, and you don't need this guide right now. It's also relatively straightforward—it's just that quest tracking isn't available for it until you progress further. I'll run through its steps below, but these will contain spoilers for how to access a later game region, so you might want to steer clear: As you progress through the Crimson Forest (2nd region), you'll hear the weeping again, giving you a nav marker that coincides with the region boss, which provides a few more answers. When you arrive in the Village of Lu (3rd region) and speak to Jewel about the weeping, she speculates that The Chord wants to tell you something, and you're directed to the northeast of Meigu Lake. You'll have to progress through Pangzhen (4th region) and defeat its main boss in the west to get the Phantom Edge that unlocks the way to Meigu Lake via the north of the town. In the northeast of Meigu Lake, y…

title: Where to find the Backstreet Courtyard Key in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Open the locked door in the backstreets of Pangzhen.
body: (Image credit: S-Game Studios) I spent a long time in Phantom Blade Zero searching for the Backstreet Courtyard Key, convinced it would unlock the inaccessible area where Old Man Gen's house is located, as well as the third acolyte scarecrow. Turns out, that gate doesn't lead to either. If you're searching for that key with that in mind, you instead need to acquire the Flaming Mane phantom edge from the region boss and follow the main quest to repair it with Lei Dang, then use it to burn the barrier by the Pond of Fading Song bell where you fought Gu Wanyue, The Wailing Wraith. This leads around the back and lets you access both quest locations. Now, if you're here because you're genuinely interested in the Backstreet Courtyard Key, you won't get it until you reach the Mountain of Imprisonment area. Speak to the couple near the Shrine Outer Gate, complete the Ledger of Atonement quest by finding the ledger in the caves below, and then speak to the woman there to start the Bai Xue quest, getting you the key. The location is mainly relevant to this specific quest and doesn't hold much value beyond it. If you're wondering how to reach the Mountain of Imprisonment, you'll need to comp…

title: Where to find The Banyan's Heart in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Acquire this special material to unlock new skills.
body: You'll need The Banyan's Heart in Phantom Blade Zero to unlock certain skills like Fluid Form Level 2, Quick Remedy, or Opening Strike. You can get your first Banyan Heart towards the end of the Crimson Forest area, just after you activate the Parting Mists bell, after you fight Stone Fist Iron Fever—it's basically impossible to miss: Drop down from the Parting Mists bell and head across to the island with the tree directly ahead of you. Interact with it to be transported into The Banyan Tree's trial realm. You'll have to defeat three waves of enemies, culminating in Jing Ye, the bleed bandit boss from earlier in the Crimson Forest. Similar to the Long Pillars, if you die, there is a bell you can use, and as with boss phases, if you complete a stage of the trial, it's done and you'll start at the next. I genuinely think Jing Ye is the most annoying boss I've encountered so far. I recommend equipping the Cavalrybane accessory you can get in the Crimson Forest for more damage when he's mounted, plus the Shieldbreaker talisman if you found it in the Weeping Creek Valley to break his shield quicker. Other than that: Draw him away from the two other enemies who spawn. Dodge his bleed p…

title: How to beat Hua, Deadly Betrothed in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Defeat this phantom bride below the Valley Sha-Chi tower.
body: Hua, Deadly Betrothed is one of the first optional bosses in Phantom Blade Zero , below the Sha-Chi Tower in the Weeping Creek Valley, but you'll have to defeat her if you want to find a Flesh Lily for Yu'er. The trickiest part of this fight is avoiding Hua's spider lilies, but here are some tips to defeat her, plus a video above of my successful run employing these strategies: Avoid her lilies and stay mobile : There are three types of lily in this fight: Those that bloom periodically and when she attacks, before exploding. Those that patrol the arena and explode when they all meet in one spot. White lilies she fires out that track and stun you, letting her follow up with a red grab attack. These are the most dangerous, especially as she teleports to attack you after she fires them. Make some distance and either dodge or block them when you're sure she isn't attacking. Learn to counter her red grabs : This is Hua's deadliest attack, when she flashes red, grabs you and deals a lot of damage with a decapitating slash. If you're struggling to react, remember, red attacks are right bumper to parry, blue attacks are left, though you can just press both if it's less confusing. Hua also…

title: Where to find the Flesh Lily in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Track down this rare flower to help Yu'er's father.
body: Finding a Flesh Lily for Yu'er is the first sidequest you'll encounter in Phantom Blade Zero , but you can't complete it until a few areas and bosses later. You can find the Flesh Lily below the Sha-Chi tower, an area you reach after arriving at the outpost and beating Peng Meng. Specifically, it's accessible from the Valley Sha-Chi Tower 1st Floor bell when you arrive at the base of the tower, though you'll have to fight a boss to get it. Follow the video above, or: From the Valley Sha-Chi Tower 1st Floor bell, ascend the stairs and then circle around the right side of the tower. Drop down the hole at the back and slide down the long wooden ramp into the cavern filled with red spider lilies. Turn left and head up the slope into the lily-filled clearing above. When you arrive in the clearing, a cutscene will play, and you'll find yourself fighting Hua, Deadly Betrothed. She's relatively tricky, but this Hua boss guide offers more tips for defeating her, which will get you her powerful Scarlet Wraithblade. You'll also find the Twinned Flesh Lillies item on the corpse by the pavillion where she was standing at the start of the fight. After you defeat Peng Meng, Yu'er appears next to…

title: Can you name the horror games these deeply unpleasant bathrooms are from?
summary: Bring holy water and Clorox wipes
body: The second scariest thing about any haunted house is always the bathroom, with the first obviously being closet doors that are ever so slightly ajar. Public restrooms are scary in general, but homes always have some manner of bathroom cryptid playing peekaboo with the shower curtain, and I can't handle that. More quizzes! (Image credit: Future) Want to keep testing your knowledge of gaming trivia? We've got loads more PC Gamer quizzes , on everything from healthbars to weird currencies to absurd patch notes. It's also where a lot of horror games love to send us, whether it's for a good ol' fashioned jumpscare from apparitions in a mirror or just a particularly unsanitary commode. There's also the underrated sink baby gag from P.T., so you can't even wash your hands without developing a complex. You've got 12 minutes to identify the 14 horror games these gross restrooms are from. When you're done, let us know how you did! title: One of the best quests in Baldur's Gate 3 is also its scariest, and it doesn't have anything to do with ghosts or vampires
summary: Drowning in consequences.
body: Baldur's Gate 3 has a lot of quests that feel resonant around this particularly spooky time of year. It has an elaborate haunted house that unravels a sordid saga of love and betrayal. It has vampires and vampire hunters. It has shadow monsters that hide in plain sight until you trigger an ambush. But none of these segments got my heart pumping as much as my trip down to the Iron Throne. Presented by (Image credit: Torn Banner) This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 . Aesthetically, this return to our old pal Sarevok's sunken stomping grounds isn't nearly the creepiest or most unsettling part of the adventure. That would probably have to go to the Mindflayer Colony below Moonrise Towers. It's a murky prison full of evil fish men and some unpleasant surprises, but the somewhat BioShock-esque decor isn't doing the heavy lifting on its own. The key here is that it's one of the only places Baldur's Gate 3 flips our mechanical expectations on their head to create genuine panic and terror. The reason I feel my stomach starting to churn every time I approach this quest on a new playthrough is that diabolical timer. If you haven't been here before, I'll keep it light on …
